title: Reproduce the released prediction-loss summary; recover the unreported class definitions
statement: The author’s three publicly released prediction CSVs reproduce the stated mean log-loss gains exactly: 0.041520, 0.064377 and 0.041292 nats per token across 45, 45 and 44 test folios respectively. Their listed test-folio sets are pairwise disjoint. In an independently seeded 10,000-replicate paired whole-folio bootstrap of these released losses, all three intervals exclude zero; deleting any single test folio also leaves each gain positive. This audits the aggregation of the released outputs, not their production: the files contain no word strings or class definitions and cannot establish preprocessing, model training, source bytes, or replication on other witnesses.
check: Obtain the 18 class definitions, preprocessing, partition and model implementation or a comparably complete frozen specification. Reconstruct from hash-verified source IVTFF, then test across matched lines of genuinely independent witnesses with folio-grouped training and an untouched final evaluation partition. Independently repeat position-matched predecessor controls and quantify uncertainty without treating these released model predictions as independent model fits.
source: Matthew Dominik, Line-Conditioned Orthographic Organization in the Voynich Manuscript (2026), https://zenodo.org/records/23407412. Files predictions_rep1.csv, predictions_rep2.csv and predictions_rep3.csv are author-provided loss outputs, each verified against the deposit’s MD5 and reported SHA-256.
method: For each CSV, group baseline_loss - model_loss by its folio identifier and compute the token-weighted mean. Sample the same number of folios with replacement 10,000 times using Python random.Random seeds 42025, 42026 and 42027, preserving the two losses together and weighting sampled folios by their original token counts; report percentile entries 249 and 9749. For leave-one-folio-out, recompute the token-weighted mean after omitting each folio. Compare sets of folio identifiers across files. No model was retrained and no external held-out pages were accessed.

reproduce.command: Save script as /tmp/reproduce_author_audit.py and run python3 /tmp/reproduce_author_audit.py (downloads 0.9 MB from Zenodo).
reproduce.script:
import csv,random,json,math,hashlib
from urllib.request import urlopen
from collections import defaultdict
paths=['https://zenodo.org/api/records/23407412/files/predictions_rep%d.csv/content' % i for i in range(1,4)]
expected=['380ac745f59a984244b219ed218ba433','6ea27bf54de02598847ad1b53b87b09e','e80709783db8d0bfa70d84e826854eb7']
byrep=[]; out=[]
for j,(p,h) in enumerate(zip(paths,expected),1):
 raw=urlopen(p,timeout=30).read();assert hashlib.md5(raw).hexdigest()==h
 g=defaultdict(list)
 for r in csv.DictReader(raw.decode().splitlines()):
  assert int(r['replication'])==j
  g[r['folio']].append(float(r['baseline_loss'])-float(r['model_loss']))
 d={f:(len(v),sum(v)) for f,v in g.items()};byrep.append(d)
 n=sum(x[0] for x in d.values()); gain=sum(x[1] for x in d.values())/n
 rng=random.Random(42024+j); ids=sorted(d);boots=[]
 for _ in range(10000):
  selected=rng.choices(ids,k=len(ids)); boots.append(sum(d[i][1] for i in selected)/sum(d[i][0] for i in selected))
 boots.sort();loo=[(sum(x[1] for f,x in d.items() if f!=i)/sum(x[0] for f,x in d.items() if f!=i)) for i in ids]
 out.append({'rep':j,'tokens':n,'folios':len(ids),'gain':gain,'bootstrap_95':[boots[249],boots[9749]],'folios_positive':sum(s>0 for n,s in d.values()),'folios_negative':sum(s<0 for n,s in d.values()),'leave_one_folio_gain_range':[min(loo),max(loo)],'sha256':hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()})
inter=[]
for i in range(3):
 for j in range(i+1,3):
  a,b=byrep[i],byrep[j]; shared=sorted(a.keys()&b.keys());inter.append({'replications':[i+1,j+1],'shared_test_folios':len(shared),'overlap_fraction_of_smaller':len(shared)/min(len(a),len(b))})
print(json.dumps({'result':out,'test_folio_overlap':inter},indent=2))

limitations: These CSVs reflect the author’s original test outputs, already used in the preprint, so this is a public-data audit rather than a new held-out experiment. Disjoint test folios do not prove independence of training sets, model choices, underlying scribal sources or folio measurements. The bootstrap treats folios as exchangeable and does not account for training/model-selection uncertainty. IT and RF were not evaluated here, and the model cannot be independently replicated from the loss files. The three confidence intervals are descriptive; no multiplicity correction is claimed. The deposited CSVs do not give placebo trials or substantiate preprocessing provenance.
